messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: canary v5.0.2 CPU steal on inference-workers +35% vs baseline. Autorevert scheduled in 4m. Details: https://telemetry/cpu-steal?span=5m
frank: Noted. Looks concentrated on region us-west-2 and on kernels with the new scheduler flag. Can we pause autorevert while we triage targeted route-level pin?
anya: Oncall. Prefer targeted route pin for text-generation-usw rather than full revert — fewer customers impacted. Who can run that?
mel: I'll prepare the rollback comms if we need to widen it. Suggest suppressing auto for 15m so we can validate.
ops-bot: Autorevert countdown: 240s. Request suppression needs operator approval.
frank: Proposal: 1) suppress autorevert 2) pin route text-generation-usw in canary to v5.0.1 3) drain v5.0.2 pods in problematic AZ 4) monitor CPU steal and latency for 15m 5) escalate to full revert if other routes degrade.
anya: Command to run: ```
rls route-pin --env canary --route text-generation-usw --to v5.0.1 --reason "cpu-steal spike"
```
ops-bot: Operator override from frank accepted. Autorevert suppressed for 15m.
ops-bot: Executing: rls route-pin --env canary --route text-generation-usw --to v5.0.1
ops-bot: SUCCESS: route pinned. Traffic rebalanced.
mel: Sending CS note: "We observed elevated CPU contention for a canary subset in US-WEST. Rerouting a small portion of traffic to the previous version while we investigate. Monitoring and will update in 15m."
frank: Observing CPU steal drop on pinned route, other routes steady. Keeping pin for now. Will follow up with postmortem ticket RL-5502.
anya: Good work. If metrics stay stable for 20m, unpin and resume gradual rollout with scheduler-flag disabled in next candidate.
mel: Filing brief to product and legal about the kernel flag change and potential rollback impact.
deploy-bot: NOTE: autorevert suppression will expire at +15m if not extended.
frank: Extending suppression not necessary now, we have manual control. Closing thread after monitoring window. Thanks all :thumbsup:
